subject: Onboarding kickoff: model shortlist, context requirements & preliminary token projections
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@helio.tech>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@helio.tech>
Date: Sun, 14 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Kickoff + model constraints & traffic snapshot

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the HelioTech product and data team are excited to move forward. Attached is a preliminary workload snapshot (csv in the sheet) that shows our current daily inbound document volume, average document sizes, and our top 6 routes. A few quick notes up front: 

- Primary use case: automated summarization + retrieval-augmented answers for customer support (priority route).
- Peak patterns: heavy daytime spike (US PST) and weekend taper.
- Security: we'll need a Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC peering; SOC2 evidence will be requested in the SOW.

Initial questions for handoff to CS/implementation:
1) Given the sample doc sizes, do you expect 4k vs 32k context models to be necessary for the priority route?
2) Can you give a ballpark token burn per summarized document and a near-term (first 90 days) token forecast so our procurement folks can size the commitment?
3) Any immediate blockers you foresee for a November pilot?

I've attached the workload snapshot (helio-workload-snapshot-20271114.xlsx). Happy to hop on a quick handoff call if that helps.

Thanks,
Elena
Product Lead, HelioTech


--
Attachment: helio-workload-snapshot-20271114.xlsx (spreadsheet, 4 sheets: routes, doc-samples, hourly-profile, metadata)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Hi Elena — thanks for the snapshot, that was helpful. Looping in Monica (CS lead) and Jordan (solutions) for the implementation handoff.

Quick answers up front, then Monica will follow with a concise shortlist and estimates:
- Context: priority route (support summarization + RAG) looks like a mix of medium-length docs (~1.5k tokens) with some long transcripts (~8–12k tokens). We should size for at least a 16k context candidate for pilot; 32k optional if you prefer fewer chunking steps and better long-doc fidelity.
- Token burn: rough starter estimate ~1.2–1.6x of raw doc tokens for single-pass summarization + answer generation (depends on prompt length and RAG overhead).
- Pilot blockers: network/VPC details and DMZ routing for private endpoints — procurement and infra will need a short checklist.

Monica — can you share the model shortlist (2–3 candidates) with the expected latency/cost tradeoffs and a 90-day token projection based on the attached sheet? Jordan, please add anything about batching/context-window recommendations.

Happy to set up a 30-min handoff call tomorrow if that helps move procurement.

Best,
Grace
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Elena Park <elena@helio.tech>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Kickoff + model constraints & traffic snapshot

Hi all — quick model shortlist and the requested 90-day token projection based on the HelioTech sheet. I kept things pragmatic: focus on predictable latency and cost for the pilot, with an easy upgrade path to higher context if accuracy needs it.

Model shortlist (pilot candidates):
1) redwood-embed-med (causal backbone, 16k) — best latency/cost balance for summarization pipelines where we chunk and RAG. Good for most docs, cheaper than higher context variants.
2) openbig-16k-q4 (open model, 16k quantized) — lower inference cost, slightly higher latency variance; good if Helio is cost-sensitive.
3) redwood-large-32k (32k context) — recommended only if you want to avoid chunking for transcripts; higher per-token cost but simplifies prompt engineering.

Assumptions used:
- Pilot traffic: 2,500 priority-route docs/day, average 3,200 tokens per doc (based on attached sample).
- Summarization workflow: prompt + RAG retrieval ~ generation length 400 tokens on average.
- Retries / post-processing multiplier: 1.05 (small buffer).

90-day token projection (priority route only):
- daily input tokens: 2,500 * 3,200 = 8,000,000 input tokens/day
- daily generation tokens: 2,500 * 400 = 1,000,000 generation tokens/day
- total daily tokens = 9,000,000; 90-day = 810,000,000 tokens

Cost/latency notes (pilot):
- redwood-embed-med (16k): expected p50 latency ~240–350ms per request under burst-friendly batch settings; approximate unit economics best for this profile.
- openbig-16k-q4: p50 ~320–450ms; cheaper per-token, test for hallucination/regression on a small eval set.
- redwood-large-32k: p50 ~480–700ms; recommended only if transcript quality loss from chunking is unacceptable.

Next steps I'm proposing:
- Wrap these estimates into a lightweight M.A.P. (mutual action plan) for procurement (I can draft).
- Run a 2-day eval on a 100-doc holdout to compare redwood-embed-med vs openbig-16k-q4 for fidelity.
- Jordan to share recommended batching batch sizes and KV cache windowing to meet the latency SLO.

Attachments: redwood-model-shortlist-matrix.pdf (shortlist + per-route economics table)

Thanks,
Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Elena Park <elena@helio.tech>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Kickoff + model constraints & traffic snapshot

Adding the technical tradeoffs and an ops-minded approach:

Operational notes for implementation team:
- Context window: start with 16k model and aggressive prefix/KV caching for short Q&A flows. Store RAG chunks at 4k chunk size with overlap=0.2 for retrieval quality.
- Batching: target inter-request batching window 8–12ms on Dedicated to hit throughput without violating p95 latency SLOs; use dynamic batch sizing based on request size distribution.
- Quantization and fallbacks: enable q4 variants for non-priority routes; set fallback policy to openbig-16k-q4 when redwood-embed-med queue depth exceeds threshold.
- Token accounting: enable token-level tracing per route and add alert when projected weekly burn > 5% above forecast to trigger throttling or temporary model swap.

Pilot runbook (short):
1) Day 0–2: 100-doc eval (compare fidelity + latency).
2) Day 3–7: pilot with 2,500 doc/day slice (feature-flagged route), observe token burn and latency metrics.
3) Week 2–4: instrument prompt perturbation set for regression alerts.

I'll add these operational settings to the onboarding handoff doc and send a calendar invite for a 30-min kickoff tomorrow at 10am PST if that works for everyone.

--
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
